title: Platform systems & services - playbook, how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap (Q1 2026)
author: Elena Morales
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical Platform Engineering playbook for systems & services. It consolidates: system ownership and service inventory, standard how-tos for common platform tasks, dashboard and alert definitions, runbooks for high-severity incidents, retrospective guidance, and the near-term roadmap (Q1 2026). Intended audience: platform engineers, SRE, on-call, and partnering product teams.

Goals
- Ensure consistent operational practices across clusters and regions.
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to recover (MTTR) by providing clear runbooks and dashboards.
- Maintain SLOs for core platform APIs and critical services.
- Provide an actionable roadmap and owners for Q1 2026 improvements.

1) Service inventory & ownership
- Core services (owners):
  - routing-proxy (owner: platform-routing team)
  - runtime-api (owner: serving-runtime)
  - batch-ingest (owner: infra-data)
  - telemetry-collector (owner: observability)
  - deployment-manager (owner: platform-deploy)

Each service entry in the system registry must include: primary_owner, secondary_owner, SLOs, tags, and runbook link. See "How to update service registry" below.

2) SLOs & error budget policy (summary)
- runtime-api: availability 99.95% monthly, p99 latency < 250 ms for 0-1024 token requests.
- routing-proxy: availability 99.99% monthly, p95 latency < 30 ms.
- telemetry-collector: availability 99.5% monthly (best-effort ingestion).

Error budget burn policy:
1. If burn > 25% in a 7-day window -> on-call lead review and mitigation plan.
2. If burn > 50% -> pause risky rollouts and notify Platform leadership.

3) Dashboards & alerts (how-to and definitions)
Overview: All platform dashboards are hosted in Grafana under the "Platform" folder. Panels are reusable queries from the observability metrics catalog. Panels are tagged with service and owner.

Key dashboards (path in Grafana)
- Platform Overview (grafana/platform/overview): cluster capacity, API QPS, total cost-per-hour.
- runtime-api - Service Health (grafana/runtime-api/health): success rate, latency heatmap, active connections.
- routing-proxy - Latency & Errors (grafana/routing-proxy/latency): p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate by backend.
- Autoscaler - Utilization (grafana/autoscaler/util): queue depth, scale events, thundering events.

Alert catalog (examples)
| Alert name | Expression (summary) | Severity | Owner | Escalation |
|------------|----------------------|----------|-------|------------|
| runtime_api_high_latency | p95(latency) > 250ms for 5m | P1 | serving-runtime | on-call -> team lead -> platform SRE |
| routing_proxy_5xx_spike | rate(5xx) > 1% for 2m | P1 | platform-routing | on-call -> owner -> infra director |
| autoscaler_failed_scale | scale failures >= 3 in 10m | P2 | platform-autoscaler | on-call -> dev on call |
| telemetry_backlog_growth | queue_size > 10k for 15m | P2 | observability | on-call -> observability eng |

Alerting best practices:
- No more than 3 alerts per service for P1; tune thresholds to signal actionable work.
- Alerts must include runbook link and play URL. Use the alert labels: owner, service, priority.

4) Runbooks (canonical steps)
Template for all runbooks (must be present at top of each runbook page):
1. Title and service path
2. Pager and escalation matrix
3. Quick triage checklist
4. Reproduction steps and key dashboards
5. Mitigation steps (ordered)
6. Post-incident cleanup and rollback procedures
7. Postmortem link and RCA owner

Example: runtime-api high latency (P1)
- Pager: rotation platform-oncall@redwood.com, mobile pager for primary.
- Quick triage: check Platform Overview -> runtime-api health -> active request histogram.
- If p99 > 500ms and errors rising: 1) Identify recent deploys (deployment-manager) 2) Check KV cache saturation 3) Increase autoscale target by 20% (if safe) 4) Temporarily divert traffic to a warm fallback model variant.
- Mitigation CLI examples:
  - kubectl -n runtime-api get pods --selector=version=stable
  - kubectl -n runtime-api logs <pod> --tail=200 | grep "ERROR"
  - ./deployment-manager rollback --service runtime-api --to-version v2026.01.10

5) How-tos (commonly used procedures)
- How to update a dashboard:
  1. Fork the panel in Grafana, add annotation describing change + ticket ID.
  2. Test query with 30d/7d window.
  3. Submit for review (owner + observability) and merge via grafana-as-code PR.

- How to add a new service to the registry:
  1. Open platform-service-registry.yaml in the infra repo.
  2. Add entry with keys: name, owner, secondary_owner, slos, tags, runbook_link.
  3. Run make registry-validate && make deploy-registry.

- How to onboard a new on-call engineer:
  1. Read this playbook and the oncall checklist.
  2. Shadow two incidents.
  3. Complete certification: oncall-quiz (internal).

6) Retrospectives & postmortems (guidance)
- When to run: any P1/P0 incident or repeated P2 incidents with systemic root cause.
- Template: summary, timeline, impact, root causes (singular), contributing factors, mitigation, action items, owners, due dates.
- Follow-up: create a ticket for each action item, tag with "retro-action" and review in the next team sprint.

Recent retrospective highlights (Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026)
- Issue: autoscaler misconfiguration caused under-provisioning for batch-ingest on 2025-12-03.
  - Root cause: default cooldown set too high for bursty workloads.
  - Action: reduce cooldown to 30s and add synthetic load test. Owner: infra-data (done).
- Issue: telemetry ingestion spikes caused Grafana dashboard lag on 2026-01-18.
  - Action: partition telemetry topics by region and increase retention for metrics-store. Owner: observability (in progress).

7) Roadmap (Q1 2026 priorities)
- Q1 theme: "Resilience & Observability"
  - M1: autoscaler rewrite: deterministic scale decisions + improved telemetry (owner: platform-autoscaler) - target: end of Feb 2026.
  - M2: unified dashboard library (grafana-as-code) - target: March 2026.
  - M3: rollout service-level tracing (open-telemetry integration) - target: March 2026.
  - M4: on-call ergonomics improvements: richer alert context and automated runbook snapshots in alerts - target: April 2026 (stretch).

8) Operational metrics and run rate
- Weekly health checks: owners must publish a 2-line status in the team channel every Monday with: SLO status, incident count, ongoing mitigations.
- Monthly review: platform leadership reviews error budgets and cross-team dependencies.

9) Governance & change management
- Major infra changes (schema migrations, autoscaler changes, control-plane upgrades) must follow the change-management template: design doc -> canary -> monitored rollout -> rollback plan.
- All changes that affect SLOs must be flagged in the release notes and communicated 72 hours prior.

10) Appendix: useful links & commands
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/platform
- Pager duty: https://pagerduty.internal/incidents
- Service registry: git@github.com:redwood/platform-infra.git//registry/platform-service-registry.yaml
- Common commands:
  - kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l app=<service>
  - ./deployment-manager status --service <service>

Contacts & ownership
- Platform on-call rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com
- Platform lead (roadmap): Elena Morales (elena.morales@redwood.com)
- Observability lead: Priya Singh (priya.singh@redwood.com)

Document maintenance
- Owner: eng-platform (Elena Morales)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1 incident with impact > 1 hour.
summary: Canonical platform engineering playbook consolidating systems and services inventory, how-tos, dashboards & alert definitions, runbooks, retrospectives, and the Q1 2026 roadmap.
